ety.text: Hindi verb set गुँथना (gũthnā) गूँथना (gū̃thnā) गुँथवाना (gũthvānā) Inherited from Prakrit 𑀕𑀼𑀪𑀇 (gubhaï), 𑀕𑀼𑀳𑀇 (guhaï), from Sanskrit गुफति (gupháti, “strings together”). Contaminated by Prakrit 𑀕𑀁𑀣𑀇 (gaṃthaï) which derives from Sanskrit ग्रन्थयति (grantháyati, “ties”). Cognate with Nepali गुथ्नु (guthnu), Odia ଗୁନ୍ଥିବା (gunthibā), Maithili गुँथब (gũthab) and Marathi गुथणें (guthṇẽ). Doublet of गुहना (guhnā), गुतना (gutnā), and गूँधना (gū̃dhnā).

s.g: alternative form of गूँधना (gū̃dhnā, “to plait, knead”)
paternal uncle-in-law; husband's or wife's paternal uncle
ploughing; ploughed land; a cultivator's holding
tenure of, or rent paid by, a cultivator

ety.text: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀚𑁄𑀢𑁆𑀢 (jotta), from Sanskrit योक्त्र (yóktra, “rope, thong, halter”). Doublet of योक्त्र (yoktra).

s.g: a beam or ray of light, the light or flame of a lamp or candle, a halo
a lamp (as placed before an idol)

ety.text: Semi-learned borrowing from Sanskrit ज्योतिस् (jyotis). First attested as Old Hindi जोति (joti). Doublet of ज्योति (jyoti).

x: कर्मचारियों के संघ ने अपनी मांगों को लेकर जनपद अधिकारी को एक संयुक्त ज्ञापन सौंपा।
भारत और जापान के बीच स्वास्थ्य और चिकित्सा उपकरणों के क्षेत्र में सहयोग ज्ञापन का आदान-प्रदान हुआ।
मंत्रालय द्वारा जारी नए ज्ञापन के अनुसार सभी सरकारी कार्यालयों के समय में परिवर्तन किया गया है।

ety.text: From दम (dam, “breath, life”) + तोड़ (toṛ, “breaking”) + रहना (rahnā, “to remain”), meaning to be breaking life. See also दम तोड़ना (dam toṛnā)
Borrowed from Classical Persian درد (dard), from Middle Persian dlt' (dard, “pain”). Compare Bengali দরদ (dorod), Punjabi ਦਰਦ (darad).
Borrowed from Classical Persian دلدار (dil-dâr). By surface analysis, दिल (dil) + -दार (-dār). Cognate with Bengali দিলদার (dildar).
Borrowed from Classical Persian دیوان (dēwān, dīwān), from Middle Persian d(p)ywʾn' (dēwān, “archive, collected writings”). Doublet of लिपि (lipi).
